# C6 — Unnecessary Memory Usage

*Level 1 card. 7 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Patterns that allocate, copy, retain, or leak memory beyond what the workload requires, increasing garbage collection overhead, memory-bus traffic, and system energy consumption. This includes creating more objects than needed (unnecessary creation), copying data when in-place operations or references suffice (unnecessary copying), materializing lazy sequences into full collections prematurely (unnecessary materialization), retaining oversized structures when compact representations would work (oversized retaining), pre-allocating far more capacity than typical usage (over-allocation), failing to release system resources (leaked handles), and mutable default arguments that accumulate state across calls (leaking defaults).

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C6.S1** | Unnecessary Object | create fewer objects -- reuse one, or use a literal, or do not create it at all | yes, scales with input |
| **C6.S2** | Unnecessary Copying | use a reference, a view, a slice or an in-place operation instead of copying | yes, scales with input |
| **C6.S3** | Unnecessary Data Materialization | produce the sequence lazily when it is consumed once and never indexed | yes, scales with input |
| **C6.S4** | Oversized Data Retaining | retain the smallest thing that answers the later question | **no — advisory only** |
| **C6.S5** | Over-Allocation | size the buffer to the workload, or let the container grow | **no — advisory only** |
| **C6.S6** | Leaked Resource Handles | acquire the resource in a `with` statement so it closes deterministically | **no — advisory only** |
| **C6.S7** | Leaking Mutable Default Arguments | default to `None` and create the mutable object inside the body | yes, scales with call count |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C6.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S4.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S5.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S6.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S7.md`

## Telling this category from its neighbours

These come up often enough to check before you commit:

- **C6.S1 vs C5.S3 Over-Provisioned Data Type** — C6.S1 changes how *many* objects exist.  C5.S3 keeps the count and makes each one lighter -- `__slots__`, a namedtuple, a tuple instead of a dict.  If the repair changes a count, it is C6.S1.
- **C6.S1 vs C3.S3 Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup** — C3.S3 is about a creation being *per iteration* when it could be hoisted; C6.S1 is about objects that need not exist at all.  If the loop is incidental to the finding, it is C6.S1.
- **C6.S2 vs C5.S4 Unnecessary Representation Change** — C6.S2 removes a *copy of the same representation*.  C5.S4 removes a *conversion between representations*.  `list(xs)` where `xs` is already a list is C6.S2; `list(generator)` is C5.S4.
- **C6.S2 vs C10.S3 Missing Bulk Primitive Usage** — An element-by-element copy loop replaced by `extend` or a slice fits both.  Report C6.S2 when the point is the redundant duplication and C10.S3 when the point is the unbatched per-element call.
- **C6.S3 vs C5.S4 Unnecessary Representation Change** — Decide by what the patch touches.  C6.S3 *changes the producer* from eager to lazy: `[f(x) for x in xs]` becomes `(f(x) for x in xs)`.  C5.S4 *deletes a conversion* and leaves the producer alone: `sum(list(g))` becomes `sum(g)`.
- **C6.S3 vs C3.S5 Missing Loop Early Exit** — When the saving comes from the consumer stopping early rather than from the allocation, the finding is C3.S5.
- **C6.S4 vs C5.S3 Over-Provisioned Data Type** — C6.S4 keeps fewer *things*.  C5.S3 keeps the same things in a lighter *representation*.  Dropping fields is C6.S4; `__slots__` is C5.S3.
- **C6.S4 vs C8.S1 Missing Memoization Cache** — These pull in opposite directions and both can be right about the same cache.  C8.S1 says to store more so work is not repeated; C6.S4 says to store less so memory is not held.  Say which cost you are choosing.
- **C6.S6 vs C9.S1 Fragmented I/O Calls** — C6.S6 is about *releasing* a resource.  C9.S1 is about how many times one is used -- open once and write a thousand times rather than opening a thousand times.  If the repair moves an acquisition out of a loop, it is C9.S1 or C3.S3.
- **C6.S6 vs C3.S3 Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup** — C3.S3 hoists a per-iteration acquisition out of the loop.  C6.S6 wraps an acquisition so it is released.  A loop that both opens per iteration and never closes has one repair and both labels; pick one.
- **C6.S7 vs C8.S1 Missing Memoization Cache** — A mutable default used *deliberately* as a memo is C8.S1 done badly -- the repair is `functools.cache`, not `None`.  Read whether the sharing is load-bearing before choosing.

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from a category you have already opened is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because something drew you here, which is not the same as a smell being present.
